name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+15 district with incumbent Troy Balderson seeking re-election
Huge fundraising gap: Balderson has $1.98M on hand to Christian's $19K
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 95 percent
No polls or expert ratings; challenger has minimal campaign resources
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Balderson's roughly twenty-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the incumbent near 95 percent all point to a comfortable hold, and no evidence in the record suggests the challenger has the resources or profile to close the gap.
model.watch: An exceptionally large national wave toward Democrats combined with an undercurrent of polling error is essentially the only force that could make this race competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 12th District, covering Columbus's eastern suburbs and surrounding areas, leans about fifteen points toward Republicans. Troy Balderson, the incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a commanding financial position, with roughly $1.7 million raised and nearly $2 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Jerrad Christian, has raised under $100,000 and has little cash remaining, limiting his ability to introduce himself to voters.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price the Republican at about 95 percent. Redistricting has made the seat safer than the narrow 2018 contests that first defined Balderson's tenure. Absent an extraordinary shift in the national environment, the incumbent is heavily favored to return to Congress.
